title: Screen Directors Playhouse
paragraphs: An NBC anthology of radio adaptations of major motion pictures, often featuring stars from the films and appearances or introductions by directors associated with the original productions.
NBC film-adaptation anthology featuring major motion pictures, stars and participation by original film directors.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: NBC Theater / Screen Directors Guild (January 9, 1949 to June 24, 1949) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Screen Directors Playhouse half-hour (July 1, 1949 to November 2, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Screen Directors Playhouse hour (November 9, 1950 to September 28, 1951) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Jimmy Wallington (announcer and performer), Howard Wiley (producer, performer, and production supervisor), Bill Cairn (director, performer, and producer), Richard Allen Simmons (radio adaptor and performer), Frank Barton (announcer and performer), Milton Geiger (radio adaptor and performer), and Dan Riss (performer).
Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]].
The stories often return to romance and relationships, Hollywood film culture, war and military conflict, crime and violence, and western/frontier setting.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]], [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]], [[show|escape|Escape]], and [[show|philip-marlowe|The Adventures of Philip Marlowe]].
